ENT Clinical Note  

Subjective:  
- Presenting complaint and trigger/exposure: 5-day history of “cough and cold” symptoms; no clear trigger identified.  
- Symptom timeline and progression: Onset Saturday evening after dining out; symptoms persistent x 5 days.  
- ENT symptoms:  
  • Throat: mild sore throat; possible hoarseness attributed to loud football cheering. No throat-closing sensation, no dysphagia/odynophagia, no drooling.  
  • Nasal: runny nose/congestion with audible sniffles.  
  • Ear: “a wee bit” of dullness/blocked sensation; no significant pain.  
  • Voice change: mild hoarseness (shouting-related).  
  • No facial/lip/tongue/uvular swelling, no stridor or noisy breathing, no neck pain/swelling reported.  
- Respiratory: Reports shortness of breath without chest pain; initially stated breathing “fine,” later clarified “not good” (conflict noted).  
- Constitutional: Subjective fevers with nighttime temperature fluctuations; generalized myalgia/stiffness; appetite preserved; keeping fluids up.  
- GI: One day of mild diarrhea at onset; resolved.  
- Past episodes/treatments: None mentioned; no prior hospital/ED visits for similar.  
- Allergies: Denies known drug or food allergies.  
- Current medications:  
  • Metformin – dose/route/frequency not documented.  
  • Lisinopril – dose/route/frequency not documented.  
  • Aspirin (occasional) – dose/route/frequency not documented.  
  • No rescue medications (e.g., inhalers, antihistamines, auto-injector).  
- Social context: Lives with wife; no other household members.

Objective:  
- Observable swelling: Not visualized (telephone consult).  
- Airway/breathing: No stridor reported. Patient subjectively short of breath; no objective observation possible.  
- Mental status: Appears conversational and oriented via phone. No dizziness or syncope reported.  
- Vitals & physical exam: Not recorded.  
- Accompaniment: Wife present in household; not on call.

Assessment:  
Likely viral upper respiratory tract infection (suspected early influenza-like illness) with associated runny nose, sore throat/hoarseness, mild ear congestion, subjective fever, and mild shortness of breath. No red-flag ENT airway features (no throat swelling, no stridor). Conflict noted regarding severity of breathlessness (patient initially “fine,” later “not good”).

Plan:  
- Symptomatic management: advised rest, adequate oral hydration, regular paracetamol for fever/discomfort.  
- Conditional antibiotic prescription: Amoxicillin 1 tablet three times daily to start only if symptoms (particularly breathlessness, cough) fail to improve in 24–48 h.  
- Safety-net / escalation instructions: Seek urgent medical attention (e.g., contact GP again, NHS 24, or attend ED) for new or worsening breathlessness, chest pain, persistent high fever, inability to swallow fluids, onset of throat tightness, stridor or any facial/lip/tongue swelling.  
- Follow-up: Review with GP next week if no improvement or earlier if deterioration.  
- Preventive advice: Continue smoking reduction with vaporizer; moderation of alcohol intake recommended.  
- No discussion of epinephrine auto-injector, allergy testing, or COVID-19 vaccination documented.

● Missing clinically expected elements: objective exam of throat/ears/nose, visual airway assessment, vital signs, oxygen saturation, detailed medication doses, allergy confirmation, vaccination status.  
● Internal conflicts: Patient first said breathing “fine,” later “not good.”  
● Transcript quality: Telephone audio; conversational, occasionally tangential; clinically relevant data obtainable.
